A1.justification: Both PDFs present the same TranSUN/GTS study, with readable text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices. The original appendices can be matched across renumbering, distinguishing retained material from the new FAQ, checklist, and implementation listing.

before.justification: v1 reports original experiments on eight synthetic distributions, CIKM16, DTMart, and Indus, including ablations and online recommendation A/B tests.

after.justification: v2 retains those original results and adds NDCG evaluations, convergence-related statistics, and computational and deployment measurements.

M1.justification: The core point-estimation method remains unchanged, but Appendix A.4 introduces optional ranking losses and threshold-based fusion of original and debiased predictions. Appendix A.5 additionally specifies a probabilistic GTS variant with a learned positive scale, scoring-rule objective, and conditional-CDF output. These substantially extend the documented procedures; they do not establish that the retained experiments used modified methods.

E1.justification: The datasets, synthetic distributions, and online scenarios are retained. Appendix A.1 and Table 11 add an explicit top-10%-high-value evaluation slice on CIKM16 and DTMart. This is a limited extension of subgroup coverage; the Indus Top evaluation already existed in v1.

E2.justification: The original comparisons retain their comparator membership. Added NDCG, efficiency, and convergence analyses use existing methods, including LogMSE and OptDist. The discussion of mixture density networks and normalizing flows does not introduce a separately evaluated new baseline.

E3.justification: v2 adds NDCG@All and NDCG@10%, loss-target statistics using a three-standard-deviation outlier threshold, and resource comparisons including training throughput under the same 800-worker allocation. These supplement the evaluation protocol; the original splits, training budgets, optimizers, and model settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendices A.2-A.3 substantially extend the supplementary analyses: Table 12 compares target variance and outliers across three losses, while Table 13 adds memory and computation measurements to the existing parameter-sharing study. Deployment overhead and an OptDist convergence comparison further examine practical costs and training behavior beyond v1's analyses.

E5.justification: Both versions specify ten differently seeded repetitions for synthetic experiments and five for real-world experiments, with t-tests. The online z-tests, confidence intervals, and significance-reporting practices are retained. New target-distribution statistics do not introduce a new uncertainty-reporting procedure.

E6.justification: Existing numerical tables are retained, including v1 Tables 11-14 as v2 Tables 14-17. New Table 11 reports LogSUN NDCG@10% of 0.5904 on CIKM16 and 0.9779 on DTMart; CREAD remains best on CIKM16 NDCG@All. Tables 12-13 and Appendices A.3-A.5 add substantial convergence and resource findings, rather than demonstrating improved scores between versions under unchanged settings.

T1.justification: Appendix A.5 adds a probabilistic model assumption, scoring-rule loss, and conditional-CDF formulation in Equations 12-16. Appendix A.2 also states an SGD convergence bound under a Lipschitz assumption. The original unbiasedness derivations are retained, with the missing '= 0' in v1 Equation 26 corrected in v2 Equation 31.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the central claims of intrinsic preemptive debiasing, theoretical unbiasedness, favorable convergence, GTS generality, and successful industrial deployment. Adding the platform's DAU figure to the opening repeats information already reported elsewhere in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix A.1 expands the brief XAUC trade-off discussion into an explanation involving value-aware accuracy, abundant low-value samples, and alignment with business metrics. Appendix A.4 newly acknowledges adverse effects on transaction-count metrics. Further additions interpret convergence through target variance and outliers, identify cost-effective parameter sharing, and explain the continuing need for manual GTS configuration.

D1.justification: v1 supplied experimental settings and synthetic-data generation code; v2 adds a substantial TensorFlow-style TranSUN/GTS implementation covering branches, pooling, gradient stopping, ranking losses, and prediction fusion. It also documents threshold selection, GTS tuning guidance, and operational resource measurements. The checklist still describes external code release as future work.

R1.justification: v2 adds Bottou, Curtis, and Nocedal's optimization reference and a focused comparison with mixture density networks and normalizing flows in Appendix A.5. It also explains a probabilistic connection to previously cited conditional transformation models. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain largely unchanged.

P1.justification: v2 adds a FAQ appendix, conference checklist, acknowledgments, and navigation references, alongside author-name, affiliation, and conference-header edits. The existing main narrative and appendix prose are largely retained; most expansion presents additional scientific material rather than extensively rewriting the original exposition.

P2.justification: v2 adds three tables for NDCG, convergence statistics, and resource costs, plus a formatted method-code listing. Existing Figures 1-3 and table designs remain substantially unchanged, with limited reflow and relocation of appendix tables.

improvement.justification: The added ranking and resource evidence in Tables 11-13, fuller XAUC discussion, and implementation listing improve practical assessment and reproducibility. The gains are limited by unclear attribution of the optional ranking and fusion settings to reported experiments and the absence of empirical validation for the new probabilistic variant. The original empirical foundation remains intact.
